sections.h2: What happens at the Burke County Register of Deeds after a sale closes?
sections.html:
Your signed deed lands in a permanent public ledger of Burke County land ownership, and until it is filed the buyer's title can be beaten by someone else's paperwork. The county's own description calls the office the standardized, lasting record of property ownership and transfers. Staff file deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, powers of attorney and assumed names, and they also issue vital records, marriage licenses and notary commissions.

Timing of the filing decides who wins a dispute. G.S. 47-18 says a transfer cannot be enforced against lien holders or later paying buyers until it is registered in the county of the land, and the earlier filing time wins. An unfiled Burke County deed in a closing folder gives the buyer no protection at all.

Wills and estates sit elsewhere. The register's FAQ sends estate and court-action questions to the Clerk of Court.

sections.h2: Where do I take a deed in Burke County, and what are the hours?
sections.html:
Take it to the Morganton office on South Green Street, which opens at 8 each weekday morning, closes at 5 in the afternoon and shuts on observed county holidays. Postal packages go to Post Office Box 936 in Morganton, ZIP 28680, and callers reach staff at 828-764-9340. The county's pages give two slightly different street numbers for the building, so check the door number before you send a courier.

Voters choose the Register of Deeds every second year (G.S. 161-1). Staff cannot advise on wording, so your closing attorney will draft the deed and deliver it.

  • Hand delivery in Morganton on weekdays
  • Courier or postal delivery of originals
  • Electronic filing by an approved submitter
  • Searching real estate records through the county website

sections.h2: How much will Burke County charge to file my deed?
sections.html:
For a deed, expect $26 covering the first 15 pages and $4 for every page past that, and for a mortgage or deed of trust, $64 covering 35 pages plus the same $4 per extra sheet. The county prints these in a fee schedule for FY 24-25 and cites G.S. 161-10, so they match what every North Carolina register charges.

Selected charges from the Burke County Register of Deeds fee schedule, FY 24-25
ItemCharge as printed
Instruments in general$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deeds of trust or mortgages$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page

The nonstandard surcharge hits papers that ignore the state's layout rules, so ask whoever drafts the deed to follow G.S. 161-14 on margins and type size. Cancelling a paid-off mortgage costs nothing, which is handy when a seller is clearing an old loan.

sections.h2: Who pays the state stamp tax on a Burke County sale?
sections.html:
Sellers carry this cost, and the register wants payment first. The levy comes from G.S. 105-228.30: a dollar for every $500 of value, with any leftover fraction rounded up, owed by the transferor. Burke County's fee schedule restates the rate as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 charged up to $500.

Half the money remains in Burke County's general fund, while the remainder travels to Raleigh in monthly remittances. Since the amount tracks the price in the deed, it grows with the sale. Get the stamp figure from your closing attorney's settlement statement rather than guessing.

sections.h2: Why must the Burke County tax office sign off before a deed is filed?
sections.html:
The county has a rule that the register will not take a deed conveying real property until the tax collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. Its Delinquent Tax Certification form cites G.S. 161-31, a law letting commissioners impose that rule, and the printed form was revised on April 22, 2026.

Gather these details before closing day, because the form asks for all of them:

  • GIS PIN or REID number of each parcel changing hands
  • Names of the grantor and grantee, plus the grantee's mailing address
  • The owner shown in tax records, and the street address of the property
  • The price paid and how many acres are being sold
  • Whether a single-wide or double-wide home is part of the sale
  • Whether the land sits in the Present Use Value program, and whether the buyer will keep it there
  • Any personal property that goes with the sale, from motor vehicles to boats and farm equipment

Tax staff complete a ten-year grid of owners, deferred amounts and taxes due. Call the tax administration office at 828-764-9430 or write to collections@burkenc.org. According to the register's FAQ, correcting a mistake in a recorded deed means drafting a new one, carrying it through the tax office and then filing it again.

sections.h2: Can my Burke County deed be filed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The register takes electronic documents through Simplifile and Corporation Service Company, per the county's eRecording page and FAQ. The closing firm opens a submitter account, sends the package from its own desk and receives the recorded copy digitally right after filing.

If you sign from another state, that route can cut days off the gap between signing and public ownership. Ask the attorney whether the firm files through one of these platforms and whether the tax certification is already done.

sections.h2: What is the Burke County market like, and what is the 2027 revaluation?
sections.html:
Burke County lies in the mountain region of western North Carolina and is heading into a countywide revaluation for 2027. The commissioners posted notice of a November 16, 2026 hearing on the proposed schedule of values and the present use schedule for that project, with both documents open at the tax office and on the county site.

The county website says local employers make industrial products, with technological, furniture, medical, chemical, machine component and textile manufacturers on the list. It also mentions the western campus of the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics and Western Piedmont Community College.

  • Census Bureau count of 88,655 residents and 41,669 housing units in its July 2025 estimate
  • Homeowners live in about 74.5% of homes (2020-2024)
  • Typical home value among owners: $185,400, per 2020-2024 figures
  • Middle-of-the-range rent of $884 a month and household income of $58,592
  • Land area: 506.24 square miles, per Census Bureau QuickFacts

Nearly one in four Burke residents (23.2%) is past 65, which makes the state's elderly and disabled homestead exclusion relevant locally. For 2026 the state revenue form sets that program's income cap at $38,800.

faqs.q: What will it cost to file a deed with the Burke County register?
faqs.a: Roughly $26 for a deed up to 15 pages, then $4 for each more, per the county's fee schedule. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages. The seller's stamp tax is billed apart from those fees.

faqs.q: Do I have to clear the Burke County tax office before filing a deed?
faqs.a: For a deed moving real property, yes. The delinquent tax certification form, tied to G.S. 161-31, bars the register from accepting it until the tax collector certifies no delinquent taxes. Send the form with the PIN or REID number and sale facts.

faqs.q: Does the Burke County register handle probate and wills?
faqs.a: No. The county FAQ routes estate and court questions to the Clerk of Court, listed at 828-433-3200, and the register's office stays on land and vital records.

faqs.q: Who covers the excise tax when a Burke County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller. State law makes the transferor pay the register before recording, at a dollar for each $500 of value. The settlement statement shows the exact amount.

faqs.q: Can I look up Burke County property records from home?
faqs.a: Yes, the county FAQ says real estate records are viewable online. For gaps the index leaves open, call 828-764-9340 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays.
